principle: Character growth modifies bounded aspects of expression or trait intensity through represented causes; it never silently replaces personality.
rules: Small changes may accumulate through long service, relationships, mentorship, trauma recovery, success/failure and aging when represented by events.
Large trait inversions require exceptional, explicit narrative/state causes.
Relationship warmth/trust normally changes relationship state, not global personality.
Temporary grief, fear, intoxication, fatigue, injury or acute stress belongs to current state.
Recovery may return expression toward baseline without deleting event history.
Personality evolution survives save/load and off-screen simulation.
Canonical-character research phases may inspire this model but procedural NPCs never copy a canonical arc.
examples: guarded NPC becomes somewhat more open after years of stable trusted relationships
insecure junior officer gains self-confidence after repeated competence and promotion
rule-rigid officer becomes slightly more flexible after several situations where rigid procedure caused avoidable harm
highly humorous officer becomes temporarily quiet during grief without changing humor_frequency baseline
